A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LieRA study, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. All pages were inspected: v1 ends after its references, while v2 includes appended Sections 7–10 and Tables 8–10.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original LieRA benchmark results, generated-image examples, resource measurements and ablations in Tables 1–7 and Figure 2.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments in Tables 1–7 and Figure 2, with additional experimental documentation and runtime reporting in the appendix.

M1.justification: The Lie-group multiplicative update, exponential map, first-order approximation and integration with LoRA remain unchanged in Section 4. The appendix documents implementation settings without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover VTAB-1k, COCO detection and segmentation, subject-specific image generation, commonsense reasoning and GLUE. The appendix identifies DreamBooth and Commonsense170K for existing experiments; it does not add a distinct task, domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding tables: full fine-tuning and LoRA, the ChatGPT/Series/Parallel/PISSA/MiLoRA commonsense comparisons, and PISSA/DoRA coupling experiments. Appendix Section 9 clarifies baseline provenance and ChatGPT configuration without adding a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes the stated ConvNeXt-V2-L configuration to ConvNeXt-V2-B and removes ViT-B/16; Section 5.1.2 removes LLaMA2-7B. These are limited reported configuration corrections: the retained tables already identify ConvNeXt-V2-B and contain no ViT or LLaMA2 results. They do not establish experimental reruns.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 retains the same Taylor-approximation comparison, training-cost analysis and coupling experiments with PISSA and DoRA. The generation examples also remain unchanged; the appendix adds no new ablation, robustness test or case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Table averages remain averages across tasks, without newly reported uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 1–7 and qualitative examples in Figure 2 are unchanged. Appendix Section 8 newly reports approximately 21 minutes for SDXL fine-tuning and about 30 seconds for generation with 50 inference steps. These are limited additional runtime outcomes, not improved benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the nonzero-tensor Lie-group construction, exponential-map reasoning, Taylor approximation and rank-capacity argument are retained. No additional theorem, proof, assumption or mathematical correction appears in the appendix.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: generalizing matrix-based PEFT to higher-dimensional parameters, preserving structural properties and improving adaptation across vision and language tasks. The added code statement does not change the scientific contribution claimed.

C2.justification: The explanations involving spatial locality, expressive rank capacity and the approximation–resource tradeoff remain unchanged. The existing focus on convolutional parameters and proposed future architectural extensions are retained, without new substantive limitations or interpretations.

D1.justification: v1 refers to an appendix but supplies none. v2 adds Sections 7–10 and Tables 8–10, documenting data splits, preprocessing, dataset sources, optimization hyperparameters, adaptation targets, generation procedures and hardware/timing details. It also adds a code-access link and identifies the sources of borrowed LoRA results. This substantially expands reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds citations to MAP and Weight spectra induced efficient model adaptation. The appendix adds dataset and protocol references, including DreamBooth, VTAB and LLM-Adapters. The substantive positioning relative to LoRA, FLoRA, Atom-filter and Lie-group research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains nearly verbatim and preserves the Section 1–6 organization. v2 appends four experimental-detail sections and makes limited affiliation, correspondence-marker, code-availability and model-list edits, without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds three hyperparameter tables, Tables 8–10, and reflows the text and references. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–7 retain their designs and contents. The visual changes are a limited extension of the existing presentation.

improvement.justification: The added appendix and code-access statement improve transparency and reproducibility, while the model-description corrections reduce inconsistencies with the retained tables. These are useful documentation gains. The benchmark evidence, ablations, theoretical arguments and central conclusions remain unchanged, supporting a limited overall quality improvement.
